explainedBy: Brennan confronts his own analyst across the table: he points and pushes back, she sinks under it.

storyboard.claim: Brennan is the friction; he pushes back on his own team.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Brennan pointing angrily at the analyst, who slumps worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the room tilts toward a strike, one man pushes against it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Who pushes against whom: the adviser against his own analyst.

callout.text: What's not right about our theory?

explainedBy: Brennan demands the analysts attack their own theory, the compound model between them; she is taken aback.

storyboard.claim: He demands they disprove their own theory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same pair, now with the compound model between them; Brennan talks, the analyst is surprised.
storyboard.onScreenText: What's not right about our theory?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept stage: the model of the theory appears, the analyst's face turns to surprise.
storyboard.addedInformation: The theory under attack (the compound model) is on screen.

explainedBy: The analyst now hunts for contrary evidence with a magnifier over the compound model.

storyboard.claim: Forced to look for contrary evidence, the analysts find a tiny detail.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst holding a magnifier over the compound model, Brennan watching.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The demand turns into the analysts searching.
storyboard.addedInformation: The search itself: looking closely at the compound for what does not fit.

explainedBy: The overlooked detail: a dog on the compound grounds, which the analyst points to.

storyboard.claim: Satellite imagery shows a dog pacing the compound.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst pointing, surprised, at the dog icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tiny detail the search turned up.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the detail: a dog.

explainedBy: Cause chain starts: a dog on the grounds versus devout households rarely keeping dogs.

storyboard.claim: Strictly devout Muslims of his interpretation rarely keep dogs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: Dog on the grounds -> Devout: rarely dogs.
storyboard.onScreenText: Dog on the grounds | Devout: rarely dogs
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The dog becomes the first link of an argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Why the dog matters: it clashes with who should live there.

explainedBy: The chain ends in its result: the dog contradicts the theory of who lives there.

storyboard.claim: A red flag that contradicted the whole theory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same flow gains the result label: Theory contradicted.
storyboard.onScreenText: Dog on the grounds | Devout: rarely dogs | Theory contradicted
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept flow, one more label: the effect.
storyboard.addedInformation: The consequence: the foundational theory is in doubt.

explainedBy: The mission nearly derails: Brennan slumps worried beside the compound model.

storyboard.claim: Did the dog derail the mission? It almost did.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Brennan slumping, worried, by the compound model.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the argument back to the room it shakes.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cost of the red flag: the mission almost stopped.

explainedBy: Brennan's decades of Middle East study surface a memory: he holds the book of that knowledge, struck by it.

storyboard.claim: Brennan, fluent in Arabic and a Middle East veteran, remembers a detail.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Brennan holding a book, surprised face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The same man who doubted now supplies the answer.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the expertise is carried by the book and callout.

explainedBy: The new chain: the dog in the compound links to bin Laden keeping dogs in Sudan in the 1990s.

storyboard.claim: Bin Laden did have dogs in exile in Sudan in the 1990s.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: Dog in compound -> Dogs in Sudan, 1990s.
storyboard.onScreenText: Dog in compound | Dogs in Sudan, 1990s
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The contradiction is answered by history.
storyboard.addedInformation: The historical fact that resolves the dog.

explainedBy: Result of the chain: trying to disprove the theory made it stronger.

storyboard.claim: Disproving their theory made the final theory far stronger.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same flow gains: Theory stronger.
storyboard.onScreenText: Dog in compound | Dogs in Sudan, 1990s | Theory stronger
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept flow, one more label: the result.
storyboard.addedInformation: The payoff of friction, as cause -> effect.

explainedBy: Instead of one road, the analyst points at a fork with several paths: multiple futures.

storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst pointing at the branching-road icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From one theory to many possible outcomes.
storyboard.addedInformation: One future vs several: the branching paths.

explainedBy: One future modelled: what heat and altitude do to the helicopter's lift; the analyst weighs it, worried.

storyboard.claim: If we send Black Hawks, what do heat and altitude do to rotor lift?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The helicopter icon beside the worried analyst.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The first specific future.
storyboard.addedInformation: The concrete risk: the helicopter itself.

explainedBy: The futures sorted side by side: the helicopter raid versus bombers that leave no DNA proof.

storyboard.claim: Bombers would flatten the compound and leave no DNA evidence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter: Black Hawk raid | B-2 bombers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A second option is laid beside the first.
storyboard.addedInformation: The options as separate timelines.

explainedBy: One more timeline joins: Pakistan treats the raid as war and shuts airspace.

storyboard.claim: They planned for Pakistan retaliating by shutting American airspace.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same sorter gains: Pakistan retaliates.
storyboard.onScreenText: Black Hawk raid | B-2 bombers | Pakistan retaliates
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept sorter, one more future.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dark future they also modelled.

explainedBy: Preparing for that future: airspace shut leads to building an alternate supply route.

storyboard.claim: The military spent months building an alternate supply route.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: Airspace shut -> Alternate route.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From modelling the future to preparing for it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The concrete preparation for the bad future.

explainedBy: The route completed: the Northern Distribution Network through the Baltic and Russia.

storyboard.claim: The Northern Distribution Network routed supplies through Russia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same flow gains: Via Russia.
storyboard.onScreenText: Airspace shut | Alternate route | Via Russia
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept flow, one more label.
storyboard.addedInformation: Where the backup route actually ran.

explainedBy: Tetlock's two camps of forecasters, sorted: hedgehogs and foxes.

storyboard.claim: This maps onto Tetlock's research: foxes and hedgehogs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter: Hedgehogs | Foxes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the raid to a research frame.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two types the next beats explain.

callout.text: One big theory of the world

explainedBy: The hedgehog: one big theory of the world.

storyboard.claim: Hedgehogs have one big unifying theory.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The hedgehog icon alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The first camp, defined.
storyboard.addedInformation: What a hedgehog is.

explainedBy: The fox: many small things, constantly updated, against the hedgehog's one binary future.

storyboard.claim: Hedgehogs predict one binary future; foxes know many things and update.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The fox icon alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The second camp, in contrast to the hedgehog.
storyboard.addedInformation: What a fox is.

explainedBy: The analyst points to the fox: the 2011 intelligence team worked like foxes.

storyboard.claim: The intelligence community in 2011 acted like a team of foxes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst pointing at the fox icon, pleased.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fox is tied back to the CIA team.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links the type to the people of the case.

explainedBy: The listener leading a launch smiles at only the best case.

storyboard.claim: Leading a launch, we only model the sunshine scenario.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman holding a briefcase, smiling.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the CIA to the listener's office.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the one-sided optimism is in face and words.

explainedBy: The dream at the whiteboard: revenue up 40%, promotions all round - the listener celebrates.

storyboard.claim: At the whiteboard we promise love, 40% revenue, promotions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman celebrating.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The optimism peaks.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sunshine scenario as a celebration.

explainedBy: Futures side by side: the sunshine launch and a rival halving its price the day before.

storyboard.claim: Model the future where the competitor cuts price 50%.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter: Sunshine launch | Rival cuts price 50%.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The dream gets a rival future beside it.
storyboard.addedInformation: A second, conflicting future.

explainedBy: A third future joins: the market crashes and budgets evaporate.

storyboard.claim: Model the future where the market crashes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same sorter gains: Market crashes.
storyboard.onScreenText: Sunshine launch | Rival cuts price 50% | Market crashes
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept sorter, one more future.
storyboard.addedInformation: Another conflicting future.

storyboard.claim: Tell yourself multiple conflicting stories.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same sorter closes with: Conflicting stories.
storyboard.onScreenText: Sunshine launch | Rival cuts price 50% | Market crashes | Conflicting stories
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept sorter, the summary bucket.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: names the lesson of the three futures.

explainedBy: The objection: the listener obsessively inspecting his own plan with a magnifier.

storyboard.claim: If I keep trying to disprove my own theories...
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman holding a magnifier, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The host pushes back on the method.
storyboard.addedInformation: The obsessive checking, as a deed.

explainedBy: All that modelling means the launch never happens: the listener slumps.

storyboard.claim: Modelling every disaster, I will never launch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman slumping, sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From checking to being stuck.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cost of over-planning.

explainedBy: Waiting for 100% certainty: the listener sits while the hourglass runs out.

storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman sitting worried beside a running hourglass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The stuck state, with time draining.
storyboard.addedInformation: Time lost to waiting.

explainedBy: Commentary: we can never know everything.

storyboard.claim: Startups die from delay; bounded rationality means we never know everything.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman, sad, the term on screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The answer to the objection begins.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-carried concept.

explainedBy: The parts of bounded rationality: limited time, cognitive power and data.

storyboard.claim: We have limited time, cognitive power and data.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter: Limited time | Limited power | Limited data.
storyboard.onScreenText: Limited time | Limited power | Limited data
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The concept broken into its parts.
storyboard.addedInformation: What bounded rationality consists of.

explainedBy: Bezos's rule on a certainty scale: waiting until 90% certain.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: A new frame: the 70% rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: Where the slow decider waits.

explainedBy: The cost of waiting: the clock runs while rivals pass.

storyboard.claim: At 90% you move too slowly; rivals outpace you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman slumping, worried, beside a clock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The consequence of the 90% wait.
storyboard.addedInformation: The deadline pressure.

explainedBy: Probe the uncertainty just enough: the listener examines with a magnifier, calmly now.

storyboard.claim: The goal is to probe uncertainty enough to map the boundaries.

storyboard.addedInformation: weak: probing shown by the magnifier.

explainedBy: Prediction as several paths, not one: the branching road.

storyboard.claim: Telling several possible futures prepares the mind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The branching-road icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the rule to the general lesson.

explainedBy: The book's refrain: widen the map before you choose - the listener points to the third path.

storyboard.claim: You have to widen the map before you choose.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: Kept icon; the listener steps in to take up the lesson.

explainedBy: Imagine the disaster: the listener stands afraid before smoke and fire.

storyboard.claim: Imagine standing in the smoking crater of a total disaster.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: The premortem exercise begins.

storyboard.claim: The launch failed; the helicopters crashed and the target escaped.

storyboard.relationToPrevious: weak: the crash is in the label; no violence staged.

explainedBy: The listener explains the failure to a stern board member.
